inputs.original_text: Rubenstein is right that a political resolution matters, but peace cannot rest on asking Israel to abandon a firm stance while an operation is ongoing. A government’s first duty is to protect its people and preserve order; treating security measures as the cause of the danger risks excusing those who threaten it. Rights matter, but so do public safety and the stability families need. Any lasting settlement has to take those responsibilities seriously, not make restraint by one side the whole plan.
inputs.modified_text: Rubenstein is right: a political resolution matters, but it cannot mean demanding that Israel loosen its security stance while an operation is underway. A government’s first responsibility is to protect its people and maintain order. Blaming security measures for the danger, rather than those who threaten the public, turns responsibility upside down. Rights matter, but they cannot be separated from safety and the stability families need. Any lasting settlement must take those duties seriously instead of making Israel’s restraint the entire plan.
